name: David’s Liquid Sweetener Concentrate
sub: Homemade sucralose drops · 60 mL bottle · nutrition per 1 drop, rounded
text:
YIELD
60 mL finished concentrate (about 2 fl oz)

INGREDIENTS
2½–3 g pure sucralose powder
Distilled water, enough to make 60 mL total
⅛ tsp food-grade citric acid (about 0.6 g), optional
0.06 g food-grade potassium sorbate, optional
Up to ½ tsp flavor extract, optional (vanilla, almond, or caramel)

DIRECTIONS
1. Thoroughly wash and rinse the bottle, dropper, funnel, and mixing container.
2. Place 15 mL warm distilled water in the mixing container.
3. If using potassium sorbate, dissolve it in the warm water first. Stir in the optional citric acid.
4. Add the sucralose and optional sugar. Stir until completely dissolved.
5. Add any optional flavor extract.
6. Add distilled water to reach 60 mL total finished volume. Mix thoroughly.
7. Transfer to a clean dropper bottle, cap tightly, label with the preparation date, and refrigerate.

NOTES
Use pure sucralose powder, not a spoon-for-spoon sweetener blend. Commercial liquid sweeteners vary in concentration and cannot be substituted by a fixed volume.
Citric acid adds acidity and a slight tang, and helps potassium sorbate work effectively.
Optional preservative: Potassium sorbate helps inhibit yeast and mold, especially when used with citric acid. Keep refrigerated.
Equipment: A milligram scale reading to 0.001 g is needed for these small quantities. Basic models start around $10. Calibrate before use; kitchen spoons cannot reliably measure the potassium sorbate.
Keep refrigerated with or without preservative. Shelf life has not been established for this homemade formula.
Drop size varies by bottle. Start with 2 drops per cup of coffee, stir, and increase one drop at a time. No fixed drop-to-sugar conversion has been established.
This supplies sweetness, not the bulk or texture of sugar in baking.

MACROS
Per 1 drop, rounded: 0 kcal · 0 g protein · 0 g fat · 0 g carbohydrate · 0 mg sodium. These rounded per-drop values are not whole-bottle totals.
Optional ½ tsp sugar adds approximately 8 kcal and 2 g carbohydrate to the entire 60 mL bottle. Flavor extracts and optional additives may contribute small additional amounts; their labels take precedence.
